source: Reviewed user-executed artifacts; no independent training rerun
findings: ShiftQ has lower test perplexity than uniform4_r16 in both seeds.
Random and fixed pair placement have lower test perplexity than ShiftQ in both seeds; differences are small and not a significance claim.
Adaptive-bits policy is identical to uniform4_r16: zero changed pairs. This is a degenerate ablation, not an independent mixed-bit comparison.
Calibration domain changes only 2 of 196 projection allocations.
AG News mean PPL remains worse than the unquantized reference across all fine-tuned configurations.
conclusion: The pilot supports reallocating storage between base precision and adapters, but does not establish that sensitivity-aware placement improves over matched random/fixed placement.
limitation: Only two seeds and 16384 prediction tokens per held-out domain; 0.6B with short training remains preliminary despite FAST_MODE=False.
next: Keep the heuristic fixed; run the prespecified 1.7B, 150-update, two-seed study. Do not tune the allocator on these test results.
